subject: State-Controlled Road Speed Limit Reduction
overview: The City Council approved a resolution petitioning state agencies to lower speed limits on all state-controlled roads in Medford to 25 miles per hour. The body also celebrated multiple Medford High School championship achievements and approved routine business including committee reports and victualer licenses.

items.title: Medford High School Championship Resolutions
items.summary: The Council approved resolutions congratulating the varsity rowing team, the football team, and the marching band for their respective state and league championships. Members invited representatives from the football team and marching band to appear at a future meeting.

items.title: Donation Acceptance and Meeting Records
items.summary: Approved a $100 donation from Andrew P. Castagnetti for Mystic River footbridge lights and approved the meeting minutes for November 12 and November 19, 2024.

items.title: Tree Ordinance Committee Report
items.summary: Approved a report detailing that the tree committee and public tree ordinances require further staff review, while the private tree ordinance is being handled by the zoning team.

items.title: Public Surveillance Ordinance Amendments
items.summary: Referred a discussion regarding technical amendments to the Community Control over Public Surveillance Ordinance to the Public Health and Community Safety Committee.

items.title: Public Hearing: Mystic Avenue Corridor District
items.summary: Continued the public hearing on proposed zoning amendments for the Mystic Avenue Corridor District to December 17, 2024, pending recommendations from the Community Development Board.

items.title: Common Victualer Licenses
items.summary: Approved common victualer licenses for Medford Donuts Cafe at 47 Riverside Avenue and Bunn's House at 41 Riverside Avenue.

items.title: State Highway Speed Limit Resolution
items.summary: Approved an amended resolution requesting that the Department of Conservation and Recreation and MassDOT set speed limits at 25 miles per hour on all state-controlled roads within Medford boundaries. Speakers highlighted safety concerns at dangerous intersections and the impact of high-speed traffic bleeding into residential neighborhoods.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents addressed lack of crosswalks on South Border Road, jurisdictional difficulties regarding state-controlled road maintenance, and the status of quarterly financial reports.
